title: Glycocalyx-edited mesenchymal stem/stromal cell therapy in advanced osteoporosis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: not in PMC (no full text, no supplement listing), no GEO/SRA/BioProject links, no Zenodo/Dryad hits on the DOI; text-mined accessions are only antibody and cell-line RRIDs (research resource identifiers). No data files exist to open.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract: a first-in-human trial (NCT02566655) of one infusion of glycocalyx-edited MSCs (mesenchymal stem/stromal cells) in 10 women, with bone turnover markers, bone mineral density and fracture follow-up over 2 to 5+ years.

a1_downloadable.note: No deposited dataset found (no repository links, no open supplement); patient-level clinical trial data are typically available only on request. Checked via paper_context.py, not files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Outcomes (fracture, BMD = bone mineral density) are described in the abstract but no table exists to check.

a5_enough_rows.note: 10 patients per the abstract, far below the ~400 minimum even for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Would be trivially small if it existed.

a8_label_provenance.note: Outcomes would be clinical measurements (fractures, DXA/CT bone density), not model outputs; paper text only.

honest_claim_h3: None: a 10-patient single-arm trial with no deposited data supports no ML claim.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use patients' baseline bone markers to predict which osteoporosis patients respond to an edited stem-cell infusion.
plain_idea.train_on: Baseline clinical and bone-marker measurements per patient; 10 patients per the abstract, no data deposited.
plain_idea.predict: Change in bone mineral density or fracture occurrence, measured by imaging and clinical follow-up in the trial.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would guide patient selection for cell therapy, but 10 patients cannot train or validate any model.

ml_idea: Responder prediction for MSC therapy from baseline markers; infeasible at n=10 with no public data.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Patient count (10, from abstract) already kills it.

verdict_reason: Ten-patient clinical trial with no deposited data (paywalled, no repository links); fails A1 and A5.
